text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The military-dominated National Security Council asked the government to fully implement the secular dress code under a bid to fight rising Islmaist activism.
- Turkish security forces detained seven people in Islamic dress in religious districts of Istanbul.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan hopes to square the $6 billion budget deficit from money raised by privatisation.
HURRIYET
- Erbakan, referring to the Turkish armed forces, says it is the government to decide what is a domestic threat and no other instutition.
- A leading businessmen's organisation says Turkey is heading towards the Middle Ages.
MILLIYET
- Top generals will hold an extraordinary meeting with Erbakan and the defence minister.
YENI YUZYIL
- Erbakan says joint military operations with Israel are postponed to future years.
RADIKAL
- Former ministe, Yalim Erez, says a new alternative government is ready after talks with opposition leaders.
CUMHURIYET
- A man who attacked the mass circulation paper, Hurriyet, says he was influenced by senior government politicians.
- The state-owned Emlak Bank rejected the government's plan to sell state-owned properties.
DUNYA
- Two conservative deputies are appionted to the recently-vacated trade ministry and health ministry.
- The governor of Gaziantep in the southeast says that the per capita incomes will rise by 206 percent after a huge dam projectin the region is completed.
ZAMAN
- Erbakan says no early elections will be held.
